products.name: access_request
products.description: Master reference table for access_request. Referenced by access_request_id.

attributes.name: access_request_id
attributes.description: Primary key for access_request

attributes.name: approver_employee_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the workforce employee (typically a manager or system owner) who approved or rejected the access request. Null if the request has not yet reached an approval decision.

attributes.name: associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the workforce employee record for the individual requesting or on whose behalf access is being requested. Links to the employee master in the workforce domain.

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Reference to the retail store or location for which access is being requested, when the request is scoped to a specific store or distribution center. Null for corporate-wide or system-level access requests.

attributes.name: requester_employee_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the workforce employee who submitted the access request. May differ from employee_id when a manager or HR business partner submits on behalf of another employee.

attributes.name: access_category
attributes.description: Broad category of the resource to which access is being requested: system_application (POS, WMS, HCM, ERP), physical_facility (store, warehouse, server room), data_resource (database, data lake, report), network (VPN, Wi-Fi, VLAN), reporting_tool (BI dashboards, analytics platforms).

attributes.name: access_duration_days
attributes.description: The number of days for which access is requested, calculated as the difference between expiry_date and effective_date. Null for permanent access grants. Supports time-limited access policy enforcement for contractors and seasonal retail staff.

attributes.name: access_level
attributes.description: Granular permission level being requested: read (view only), read_write (view and modify), admin (full administrative control), execute (run processes or reports), no_access (explicit denial or removal). Supports least-privilege enforcement.

attributes.name: approval_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes added by the approver during the review process. May include conditions placed on the approval, scope limitations, or instructions for the provisioning team.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the approver rendered an approval or rejection decision on the access request. Null if no decision has been made yet.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Free-text reason provided when an access request is cancelled before a final approval decision. Captures context such as employee departure, role change, or duplicate request scenarios.

attributes.name: cancelled_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the access request was cancelled. Null if the request was not cancelled. Supports lifecycle completeness in audit reporting.

attributes.name: compliance_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory or compliance framework governing the access being requested (e.g., SOX, PCI DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, OSHA). Used to route requests through appropriate compliance-aware approval workflows and to tag access grants for regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The cost center code associated with the employee's department at the time of the request. Used for labor cost allocation of IT access management activities and chargebacks.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the access request record was first created in the system. May precede submitted_timestamp if the request was saved as a draft.

attributes.name: data_classification_scope
attributes.description: The highest data classification level of the data or system resources covered by this access request: public, internal, confidential, or restricted. Drives approval workflow complexity and audit requirements.

attributes.name: department
attributes.description: The organizational department of the employee at the time the access request was submitted (e.g., Store Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources). Snapshot value for audit trail integrity.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which the requested access should be active. May be a future date for onboarding scenarios or role transitions. Supports scheduled provisioning workflows.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the requested access should automatically expire or be reviewed for renewal. Null for permanent access grants. Supports time-limited access for contractors, seasonal workers, and emergency access scenarios.

attributes.name: external_hris_transaction_reference
attributes.description: The transaction or business process ID from the Workday HCM system that triggered or is associated with this access request (e.g., a hire, transfer, or termination business process ID). Enables end-to-end traceability between HR events and access provisioning actions.

attributes.name: is_emergency_access
attributes.description: Indicates whether this request is a break-glass or emergency access request that bypasses standard approval workflows. Emergency access requests require post-hoc review and are subject to enhanced audit scrutiny.

attributes.name: is_privileged_access
attributes.description: Indicates whether the requested access is classified as privileged (e.g., system administrator, database administrator, payroll administrator). Privileged access requests require additional approval steps and enhanced monitoring.

attributes.name: job_title
attributes.description: The job title of the employee at the time the access request was submitted. Captured as a snapshot to support audit reviews even if the employee's role changes after the request is processed.

attributes.name: justification
attributes.description: Free-text business justification provided by the requester explaining why the access is needed. Required for audit and compliance purposes, particularly for elevated or sensitive access requests.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next periodic access review or certification of this access grant. Supports access recertification campaigns and compliance with least-privilege policies.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Business urgency assigned to the access request: low (routine, standard SLA), medium (elevated urgency), high (business-impacting delay), critical (emergency or break-glass scenario requiring immediate action). Drives SLA and escalation routing.

attributes.name: provisioned_by
attributes.description: The identity (username or system name) that executed the provisioning action in the target system. May be a human IT administrator username or an automated provisioning system identifier. Supports accountability in access audit trails.

attributes.name: provisioned_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the approved access was actually provisioned in the target system. Used to measure provisioning SLA compliance (time from approval to provisioning).

attributes.name: provisioning_method
attributes.description: Indicates how the access was provisioned once approved: automated (via identity governance platform or SCIM), manual (IT administrator action), or hybrid (partial automation with manual steps). Supports process efficiency analysis.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation provided by the approver when an access request is rejected. Documents the rationale for denial for audit, compliance, and requester feedback purposes.

attributes.name: related_hr_event
attributes.description: The HR lifecycle event that triggered this access request, if applicable: new_hire (onboarding provisioning), transfer (location or department change), promotion (role elevation), termination (deprovisioning), leave_of_absence (temporary suspension), rehire (re-provisioning). Null for ad-hoc requests not tied to an HR event.

attributes.name: request_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known reference number assigned to the access request at submission (e.g., AR-2024-000123). Used in communications, audit trails, and helpdesk tickets.

attributes.name: request_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the access request: draft (saved but not submitted), submitted (awaiting review), pending_approval (under manager/owner review), approved (decision made, awaiting provisioning), rejected (denied), provisioned (access granted in target system), cancelled (withdrawn by requester). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|pending_approval|approved|rejected|provisioned|cancelled — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: request_type
attributes.description: Categorizes the nature of the access request: new_access (first-time provisioning), modify_access (change to existing permissions), remove_access (deprovisioning/offboarding), emergency_access (break-glass or temporary elevated access), role_change (job role transition requiring access realignment).

attributes.name: requested_role
attributes.description: The specific role, permission set, or access profile being requested within the target system (e.g., Store Manager Read-Only, Payroll Administrator, Inventory Viewer). Aligns with role-based access control (RBAC) definitions.

attributes.name: requires_mfa
attributes.description: Indicates whether the requested access requires multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforcement. Typically true for privileged access, remote access, and access to systems containing sensitive retail or financial data.

attributes.name: review_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this access grant requires a scheduled post-provisioning review (e.g., quarterly access certification). Typically true for privileged access, emergency access, and access to sensitive financial or HR systems.

attributes.name: scope_geographic
attributes.description: The geographic scope of the access being requested (e.g., a specific store region, country, or global). Relevant for multi-region retail enterprises where access may be scoped to specific geographies for data residency or operational reasons.

attributes.name: sla_breach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the access request exceeded its SLA target fulfillment time. Set to true when the provisioned_timestamp minus submitted_timestamp exceeds sla_target_hours. Used for SLA compliance reporting.

attributes.name: sla_target_hours
attributes.description: The target number of business hours within which the access request should be fulfilled from submission, as defined by the applicable SLA policy. Varies by priority level and access category.

attributes.name: source_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the access request was initiated: self_service_portal (employee self-service), manager_initiated (submitted by a manager on behalf of a direct report), hr_system (triggered by an HR event such as hire or transfer in the HCM platform), automated_onboarding (system-generated for new hires), helpdesk (submitted via IT helpdesk).

attributes.name: submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the access request was formally submitted by the requester. This is the principal business event timestamp marking the start of the request lifecycle.

attributes.name: system_module
attributes.description: Specific module or sub-component within the target system for which access is requested (e.g., Payroll within Workday, Inventory Management within WMS, Financial Reporting within ERP). Provides granularity beyond system_name.

attributes.name: system_name
attributes.description: Name of the application, system, or platform for which access is being requested (e.g., Workday HCM, POS System, Warehouse Management System, Databricks, SAP). Free-text to accommodate the full breadth of retail enterprise systems.

attributes.name: ticket_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the corresponding IT service management ticket (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira) created to fulfill the access request. Enables cross-system traceability between the access request record and the provisioning work order.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the access request record was most recently modified. Updated on every status change, approval action, or field edit.

attributes.name: workforce_type
attributes.description: Classification of the employee's employment relationship at the time of the request: full_time, part_time, contractor, seasonal (common in retail), or vendor. Influences access policy rules, approval routing, and expiry date defaults.

attributes.name: delegated_from_access_request_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on access_request (delegated_from_access_request_id)

attributes.name: planned_impressions
attributes.description: Target number of ad impressions contracted or forecasted for this buy. Used for reach and frequency planning.

attributes.name: planned_spend_amount
attributes.description: Budgeted or forecasted spend for this media buy at the time of booking. Used for budget tracking and variance analysis.

attributes.name: rate_currency_code

attributes.name: target_audience_definition

attributes.name: view_count

attributes.name: viewability_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of impressions that met viewability standards (MRC: 50% of pixels in view for 1+ seconds for display, 2+ seconds for video). Quality metric.

attributes.name: creative_associate_id

attributes.name: creative_modified_by_associate_id

attributes.name: featured_sku_id

attributes.name: marketing_brand_id

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the internal marketing or creative team responsible for producing or managing the creative asset.

attributes.name: parent_asset_creative_asset_id

attributes.name: primary_creative_owner_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the individual user who owns or is accountable for the creative asset within the organization.

attributes.name: primary_derived_from_creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on creative_asset (derived_from_creative_asset_id)

attributes.name: alt_text
attributes.description: Alternative text description for accessibility compliance, used by screen readers and when the asset cannot be displayed.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval workflow status indicating which review gates the creative asset has passed (legal, brand, compliance).

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the creative asset received final approval and became available for campaign use.

attributes.name: asset_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or SKU-like code assigned to the creative asset for cataloging and reference across marketing systems.

attributes.name: asset_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the creative asset, used for identification and search within the Digital Asset Management (DAM) system.

attributes.name: asset_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the creative asset indicating its approval state and availability for use in campaigns.

attributes.name: asset_type
attributes.description: Classification of the creative asset by its primary format and intended use case. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: digital_banner|email_template|sms_copy|social_media_post|video_ad|print_artwork|in_store_signage|landing_page|display_ad|native_ad|audio_ad|podcast_ad|influencer_content|gif_animation|interactive_content — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: call_to_action
attributes.description: Primary call-to-action message or button text embedded in the creative asset (e.g., Shop Now, Learn More, Sign Up).

attributes.name: channel_suitability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of marketing channels for which this creative asset is suitable or optimized (e.g., email, social, display, in-store, mobile).

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting compliance review findings, legal disclaimers required, or regulatory considerations for the creative asset.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the creative asset record was first created in the DAM system.

attributes.name: creative_agency_name
attributes.description: Name of the external creative agency or vendor that produced the creative asset.

attributes.name: creative_asset_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the creative asset content, purpose, and intended use case.

attributes.name: dimensions
attributes.description: Physical or pixel dimensions of the creative asset (e.g., 1920x1080 for video, 8.5x11 inches for print, 300x250 pixels for banner).

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date after which the creative asset expires and should no longer be used in campaigns, often due to promotional expiry or seasonal relevance.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which the creative asset is valid and authorized for use in marketing campaigns.

attributes.name: file_reference_url
attributes.description: Uniform Resource Locator (URL) or Digital Asset Management (DAM) system path pointing to the stored creative asset file.

attributes.name: file_size_kb
attributes.description: Size of the creative asset file in kilobytes, used for storage management and delivery optimization.

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: Technical file format or MIME type of the creative asset (e.g., JPG, PNG, MP4, HTML, PDF).

attributes.name: is_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the creative asset has passed all regulatory and brand compliance checks (True) or has outstanding compliance issues (False).

attributes.name: is_master_version
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the master or canonical version of the creative asset (True) or a derivative/variant (False).

attributes.name: keywords
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of keywords or tags for search and discovery of the creative asset within the DAM system.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code indicating the primary language of the creative asset content.

attributes.name: license_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the usage license for the creative asset expires, after which continued use may require renewal or renegotiation.

attributes.name: licensing_terms
attributes.description: Detailed text description of licensing terms, restrictions, and usage conditions for the creative asset, including geographic and temporal constraints.

attributes.name: locale_code
attributes.description: Locale identifier combining language and country/region (e.g., en_US, fr_CA) for localized creative variants.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the creative asset record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: target_url
attributes.description: Destination URL that users are directed to when they interact with the creative asset (click-through link).

attributes.name: thumbnail_url
attributes.description: URL to a preview thumbnail image of the creative asset for quick visual identification in the DAM catalog.

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Number of times the creative asset has been deployed or used in marketing campaigns, tracked for ROI and asset performance analysis.

attributes.name: usage_rights
attributes.description: Type of intellectual property rights governing the use of the creative asset (owned, licensed, royalty-free, rights-managed, creative commons).

attributes.name: utm_parameters
attributes.description: Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) parameters appended to the target URL for campaign tracking and attribution (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term).

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the creative asset, incremented with each revision or update.

products.name: email_send
products.description: Transactional record of a bulk or triggered email send event executed through the marketing automation platform (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Klaviyo). Captures send name, campaign reference, audience segment, email template/creative asset, send timestamp, total recipients, delivered count, bounce count (hard/soft), open count, click count, unsubscribe count, spam complaint count, send type (batch, triggered, transactional), subject line, from name/address, and ESP job ID. Represents the execution event for email channel marketing.

attributes.name: email_send_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the email send event. Primary key for the email send transaction.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer segment targeted by this email send. Links to the audience definition and segmentation criteria.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent marketing campaign that this email send is part of. Links the email execution to the broader campaign strategy.

attributes.name: email_template_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the email creative template or asset used in this send. Links to the design and content structure in the marketing automation platform.

attributes.name: resend_of_email_send_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on email_send (resend_of_email_send_id)

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ecommerce.storefront. Business justification: Email campaigns target specific storefronts/brands in multi-brand retail. Essential for brand-specific email performance tracking, ensuring brand-appropriate messaging, and measuring channel-specific

attributes.name: ab_test_variant
attributes.description: The test variant identifier if this send is part of an A/B or multivariate test. Used to compare performance across test cells.

attributes.name: actual_send_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the email send job was executed by the Email Service Provider (ESP). Represents the real-world business event time for send execution.

attributes.name: bounce_count
attributes.description: The total number of emails that bounced (failed delivery). Sum of hard bounces and soft bounces.

attributes.name: click_count
attributes.description: The total number of times links in the email were clicked by recipients. Includes multiple clicks by the same recipient.

attributes.name: completed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the email send job finished processing all recipients. Used to calculate send duration and throughput metrics.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this email send record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: delivered_count
attributes.description: The number of emails successfully delivered to recipient inboxes without bouncing. Key metric for deliverability performance.

attributes.name: esp_job_code
attributes.description: The unique job or batch identifier assigned by the Email Service Provider (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Klaviyo). Used for reconciliation and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: esp_platform_name
attributes.description: The name of the Email Service Provider platform used to execute this send (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Klaviyo, Mailchimp). Enables multi-platform send analysis.

attributes.name: from_email_address
attributes.description: The sender email address used for this send. Must be authenticated and verified with the ESP for deliverability.

attributes.name: from_name
attributes.description: The sender name displayed in the recipient inbox. Represents the brand or person sending the email.

attributes.name: hard_bounce_count
attributes.description: The number of emails that permanently failed delivery due to invalid or non-existent email addresses. Indicates data quality issues.

attributes.name: is_test_send
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this send was a test or quality assurance execution rather than a production send to customers.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this email send record was last updated. Tracks changes to send status and performance metrics.

attributes.name: open_count
attributes.description: The total number of times emails from this send were opened by recipients. Includes multiple opens by the same recipient.

attributes.name: preheader_text
attributes.description: The preview text displayed after the subject line in most email clients. Used to provide additional context and improve open rates.

attributes.name: reply_to_email_address
attributes.description: The email address where recipient replies will be directed. May differ from the from_email_address for operational routing.

attributes.name: scheduled_send_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when the email send was scheduled to execute. Used for campaign timing analysis and scheduling optimization.

attributes.name: send_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name assigned to this email send event for identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: send_priority
attributes.description: The priority level assigned to this email send for queue processing and resource allocation. High priority sends are processed first.

attributes.name: send_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the email send job. Tracks the execution state from scheduling through completion or failure.

attributes.name: send_type
attributes.description: Classification of the email send execution method. Batch sends are scheduled bulk sends, triggered sends are event-driven, transactional sends are operational confirmations, automated sends are part of nurture flows, and test sends are quality assurance executions.

attributes.name: sent_count
attributes.description: The total number of email messages successfully handed off to the Email Service Provider for delivery. Represents the actual send volume.

attributes.name: soft_bounce_count
attributes.description: The number of emails that temporarily failed delivery due to issues like full mailboxes or server problems. May succeed on retry.

attributes.name: spam_complaint_count
attributes.description: The number of recipients who marked the email as spam or junk. High complaint rates damage sender reputation and deliverability.

attributes.name: subject_line
attributes.description: The subject line text displayed in the recipient inbox. Critical for open rate optimization and A/B testing analysis.

attributes.name: suppression_list_applied
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether suppression lists (unsubscribed, bounced, or blocked addresses) were applied to filter the target audience before sending.

attributes.name: target_recipient_count
attributes.description: The total number of recipients in the target audience segment at the time of send scheduling. Represents the intended send volume.

attributes.name: unique_click_count
attributes.description: The number of unique recipients who clicked at least one link in the email. Used to calculate click-through rate (CTR).

attributes.name: unique_open_count
attributes.description: The number of unique recipients who opened the email at least once. Used to calculate open rate.

attributes.name: unsubscribe_count
attributes.description: The number of recipients who opted out of future email communications via the unsubscribe link. Critical for list health and compliance.

attributes.name: utm_campaign
attributes.description: The UTM campaign tracking parameter embedded in email links. Used to identify the specific campaign or promotion in web analytics.

attributes.name: utm_medium
attributes.description: The UTM medium tracking parameter embedded in email links. Typically set to 'email' for email marketing sends.

attributes.name: utm_source
attributes.description: The UTM source tracking parameter embedded in email links for campaign attribution. Typically set to the email platform or channel name.

products.name: sms_send
products.description: Transactional record of a bulk or triggered SMS/MMS send event executed through the marketing automation platform. Captures send name, campaign reference, audience segment, message content, send timestamp, total recipients, delivered count, failed delivery count, opt-out count, click count (for tracked links), send type (promotional, transactional, alert), short code or sender ID, carrier routing, and SMS platform job ID. Represents the execution event for SMS/MMS channel marketing.

attributes.name: sms_send_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SMS/MMS send event. Primary key for the sms_send product.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer segment or audience list targeted by this SMS send. Defines the recipient population based on segmentation rules, RFM analysis, or manual list upload.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent marketing campaign that this SMS send is part of. Links this SMS execution to the broader campaign strategy and budget.

attributes.name: primary_sms_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or system account that created this SMS send record. Used for audit trails and accountability in campaign execution.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.profile. Business justification: SMS campaigns target individual customer profiles for delivery confirmation, opt-out management, and TCPA compliance tracking. New FK required as no existing profile_id column exists. Critical for mob

attributes.name: resend_of_sms_send_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on sms_send (resend_of_sms_send_id)

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ecommerce.storefront. Business justification: SMS campaigns are storefront-specific for channel-appropriate messaging and compliance. Enables storefront-level SMS performance tracking, opt-in management per brand, and ensures regulatory complianc

attributes.name: ab_test_variant
attributes.description: The variant identifier if this SMS send is part of an A/B or multivariate test. Examples include 'control', 'variant_a', 'variant_b'. Used to compare message content, timing, or audience performance.

attributes.name: actual_send_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the SMS send job was initiated and messages began transmitting to the carrier gateway. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SMS send was approved for execution. Null if no approval workflow is required or if send is still pending approval.

attributes.name: bounced_count
attributes.description: The number of messages that bounced due to permanent delivery failures such as disconnected numbers or invalid phone numbers. Subset of failed_count requiring list cleanup.

attributes.name: carrier_routing
attributes.description: The mobile carrier network or SMS gateway provider used to route and deliver this SMS send. Examples include Twilio, Vonage, or direct carrier integrations. Impacts delivery rates and cost.

attributes.name: click_count
attributes.description: The number of unique clicks on tracked URLs included in the SMS message. Measures recipient engagement and campaign effectiveness. Tracked via URL shortening and redirect services.

attributes.name: completed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the SMS send job finished processing all messages and received final delivery reports from the carrier. Null if send is still in progress or failed.

attributes.name: compliance_consent_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether all recipients in this send have verified opt-in consent on file, as required by TCPA and CTIA guidelines. Critical for regulatory compliance and audit trails.

attributes.name: conversion_count
attributes.description: The number of recipients who completed a desired action (purchase, registration, appointment booking) attributed to this SMS send via campaign tracking codes. Key ROI metric.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SMS send record was first created in the marketing automation system. Represents the initial setup or draft creation event.

attributes.name: delivered_count
attributes.description: The number of SMS messages successfully delivered to recipient mobile devices as confirmed by carrier delivery receipts. Key metric for send effectiveness and billing reconciliation.

attributes.name: failed_count
attributes.description: The number of SMS messages that failed to deliver due to invalid numbers, carrier blocks, network errors, or recipient device issues. Used for list hygiene and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: The geographic targeting scope for this SMS send, such as national, regional, or specific metro areas. Used for localized campaigns and compliance with regional SMS regulations.

attributes.name: is_mms
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this send included multimedia content (images, video, audio) making it an MMS rather than plain text SMS. MMS has different pricing and delivery characteristics.

attributes.name: media_url
attributes.description: The URL of the multimedia asset (image, video, audio file) included in an MMS message. Null for standard SMS. Used for content tracking and compliance archiving.

attributes.name: message_content
attributes.description: The actual text content of the SMS/MMS message sent to recipients. May include personalization tokens that were dynamically replaced per recipient. For MMS, this is the text portion; media URLs are tracked separately.

attributes.name: message_length
attributes.description: The character count of the SMS message content. Standard SMS is 160 characters; longer messages are segmented. Used for billing and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: message_segment_count
attributes.description: The number of SMS segments required to transmit the message. Messages over 160 characters are split into multiple segments, each billed separately. Critical for cost calculation.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SMS send record was last modified or updated. Tracks changes to send configuration, status updates, or metric refreshes.

attributes.name: opt_out_count
attributes.description: The number of recipients who replied with STOP or unsubscribe keywords in response to this SMS send, triggering automatic removal from future sends. Critical for TCPA compliance and list management.

attributes.name: platform_job_code
attributes.description: The unique job or batch identifier assigned by the SMS marketing automation platform (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Iterable) for this send execution. Used for platform-specific troubleshooting and reconciliation.

attributes.name: scheduled_send_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when the SMS send job was scheduled to execute. For immediate sends, this matches actual_send_timestamp. For scheduled sends, this represents the intended send time.

attributes.name: send_cost_amount
attributes.description: The total cost incurred for this SMS send, calculated based on message segment count, recipient count, and carrier pricing. Used for campaign ROI analysis and budget tracking.

attributes.name: send_cost_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the send cost amount. Typically USD for US operations, but may vary for international sends.

attributes.name: send_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label assigned to this SMS send event for identification and reporting purposes within the marketing automation platform.

attributes.name: send_priority
attributes.description: The priority level assigned to this SMS send for queue processing. High priority sends are processed first, used for time-sensitive alerts or transactional messages. Normal and low priority for bulk promotional sends.

attributes.name: send_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the SMS send job. Draft indicates preparation; scheduled indicates queued for future send; sending indicates in-progress; completed indicates all messages processed; failed indicates system error; cancelled indicates user-aborted.

attributes.name: send_type
attributes.description: Classification of the SMS send purpose. Promotional sends are marketing offers; transactional sends are order/account updates; alerts are time-sensitive notifications; reminders are appointment/event notifications; service messages are operational communications.

attributes.name: sender_code
attributes.description: The alphanumeric sender ID or long code phone number displayed to recipients as the message sender. Alternative to short codes, used for lower-volume or international sends.

attributes.name: short_code
attributes.description: The 5-6 digit short code number used as the sender ID for this SMS send. Short codes are leased from carriers and used for high-volume marketing sends. Provides brand recognition and opt-out handling.

attributes.name: target_country_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes representing the countries targeted by this SMS send. Used for international campaign tracking and carrier routing.

attributes.name: total_recipients
attributes.description: The total number of unique mobile phone numbers targeted by this SMS send. Represents the audience size before any delivery filtering or failures.

attributes.name: tracked_url
attributes.description: The shortened, trackable URL included in the SMS message that redirects to the campaign landing page. Enables click tracking and attribution. Typically uses bit.ly or custom domain shortener.

attributes.name: utm_campaign
attributes.description: The UTM campaign parameter embedded in tracked URLs to identify the specific campaign or promotion. Enables granular campaign performance tracking in web analytics.

attributes.name: utm_medium
attributes.description: The UTM medium parameter embedded in tracked URLs to classify the marketing medium. Typically 'text-message' or 'sms' for SMS sends.

attributes.name: utm_source
attributes.description: The UTM source parameter embedded in tracked URLs to identify the traffic source as SMS in web analytics. Standard value is 'sms' for SMS channel attribution.

attributes.name: campaign_id

attributes.name: primary_push_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user or system account that created this push notification send record. Supports audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: image_url

attributes.name: is_silent_notification

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: notification_body

attributes.name: notification_title

attributes.name: send_code

attributes.name: send_cost_amount

attributes.name: send_cost_currency_code

attributes.name: send_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title assigned to this specific push notification send for internal tracking and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: send_status

attributes.name: touchpoint_sequence_number
attributes.description: The ordinal position of this touchpoint in the customer journey (1 for first touch, incrementing for each subsequent touchpoint). Used for position-based attribution models.

attributes.name: touchpoint_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the marketing touchpoint occurred (impression served, email opened, ad clicked, SMS delivered). Critical for time-decay attribution models and customer journey sequencing.

attributes.name: touchpoint_type
attributes.description: The specific type of interaction or exposure at this touchpoint. Distinguishes passive impressions from active engagements for weighted attribution models. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: impression|click|email_open|email_click|sms_click|push_open|push_click|video_view|video_complete|social_engagement|landing_page_view|form_submit — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: user_agent
attributes.description: The browser and operating system user agent string captured at the touchpoint. Used for device and browser attribution analysis and technical compatibility tracking.

attributes.name: utm_campaign
attributes.description: The UTM campaign parameter from the touchpoint URL, identifying the specific campaign name or code. Links web traffic to campaign master data for attribution analysis.

attributes.name: utm_content
attributes.description: The UTM content parameter from the touchpoint URL, identifying the specific ad or link variant (e.g., banner_a, text_link). Used for creative-level A/B test attribution.

attributes.name: utm_medium
attributes.description: The UTM medium parameter from the touchpoint URL, identifying the marketing medium (e.g., cpc, email, social). Used for channel classification and cross-channel attribution.

attributes.name: utm_source
attributes.description: The UTM source parameter from the touchpoint URL, identifying the traffic source (e.g., google, facebook, newsletter). Standard parameter for digital marketing attribution and campaign tracking.

attributes.name: utm_term
attributes.description: The UTM term parameter from the touchpoint URL, identifying the paid search keyword that triggered the ad. Used for keyword-level attribution and SEM (Search Engine Marketing) optimization.

products.name: attribution_model
products.description: Reference master defining the attribution model configurations used to assign conversion credit across marketing touchpoints. Captures model name, model type (last-click, first-click, linear, time-decay, position-based, data-driven/algorithmic), lookback window (days), conversion event types in scope, channel weighting rules, model version, active status, and owning analytics team. Enables consistent and auditable attribution methodology across all campaign ROI reporting.

attributes.name: attribution_model_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the attribution model configuration. Primary key.

attributes.name: attribution_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who approved this attribution model configuration for production use. Part of the governance and audit trail.

attributes.name: baseline_attribution_model_id
attributes.description: Reference to another attribution model used as the baseline for comparison and incrementality analysis. Enables A/B testing of attribution methodologies and measurement of model impact on ROI reporting.

attributes.name: attribution_created_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who created this attribution model configuration. Part of standard audit trail.

attributes.name: attribution_modified_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who last modified this attribution model configuration. Part of standard audit trail.

attributes.name: primary_attribution_org_unit_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the analytics or marketing team responsible for maintaining and governing this attribution model configuration.

attributes.name: primary_superseded_attribution_model_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on attribution_model (superseded_attribution_model_id)

attributes.name: algorithmic_model_code
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the machine learning or data-driven model used for algorithmic attribution. Applicable only when model_type is 'algorithmic' or 'data_driven'. Links to the ML model registry or experiment tracking system.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this attribution model configuration was approved for production use. Part of the governance and audit trail.

attributes.name: channel_weighting_rules
attributes.description: JSON or structured text defining the credit allocation rules per marketing channel. For position-based models, specifies percentage weights (e.g., 'first:40%, last:40%, middle:20%'). For time-decay, defines the decay function parameters. For algorithmic models, references the ML model version.

attributes.name: conversion_event_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of conversion event types in scope for this attribution model (e.g., 'purchase, add_to_cart, lead_submission, store_visit'). Defines which customer actions are treated as conversions for credit assignment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this attribution model record was first created in the system. Part of standard audit trail.

attributes.name: cross_channel_enabled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this attribution model spans multiple marketing channels (omnichannel attribution). When true, touchpoints from online and offline channels are unified in the attribution path.

attributes.name: cross_device_enabled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this attribution model includes cross-device tracking and attribution. When true, touchpoints across multiple devices (mobile, desktop, tablet) for the same user are unified in the attribution path.

attributes.name: data_source_systems
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of source systems providing touchpoint and conversion data for this attribution model (e.g., 'Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Salesforce, the retail analytics platform'). Documents data lineage and integration points.

attributes.name: deduplication_window_hours
attributes.description: Time window in hours used to deduplicate repeated touchpoints from the same channel. Multiple interactions within this window are collapsed into a single touchpoint to avoid over-crediting repetitive exposures.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this attribution model configuration ceases to be active. Null for currently active models. Used for historical model retirement and version transitions.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this attribution model configuration becomes active and is applied to campaign ROI (Return on Investment) reporting and analytics. Supports temporal model versioning.

attributes.name: excluded_channels
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of marketing channels explicitly excluded from this attribution model (e.g., 'internal_traffic, test_campaigns'). Used to filter out non-customer touchpoints or internal activity.

attributes.name: included_channels
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of marketing channels included in this attribution model (e.g., 'paid_search, organic_search, email, social_media, display, affiliate, direct'). Channels not listed are excluded from attribution credit.

attributes.name: is_default_model
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is the default attribution model used for standard campaign ROI reporting when no specific model is requested. Only one model should be marked as default at any given time.

attributes.name: lookback_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days prior to conversion during which touchpoints are considered for attribution credit. Common values are 7, 14, 30, 60, or 90 days. Defines the temporal scope of the customer journey included in attribution analysis.

attributes.name: max_touchpoints_considered
attributes.description: Maximum number of touchpoints in a customer journey that will be included in attribution analysis. Touchpoints beyond this limit are truncated. Used to manage computational complexity and focus on most relevant interactions.

attributes.name: min_touchpoints_required
attributes.description: Minimum number of marketing touchpoints required in a customer journey for attribution credit to be assigned. Journeys with fewer touchpoints may be excluded or handled differently. Common values are 1 (all journeys) or 2 (multi-touch only).

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the model for system integration and reporting (e.g., 'LC_2024Q4', 'MTL_STD').

attributes.name: model_description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the attribution model's purpose, methodology, use cases, and any special considerations. Provides context for analysts and stakeholders on when and how to apply this model.

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name of the attribution model (e.g., 'Q4 2024 Last-Click Model', 'Multi-Touch Linear Attribution').

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the attribution model. Active models are in production use; inactive models are paused; draft models are under development; archived models are retained for historical reference; deprecated models are superseded by newer versions.

attributes.name: model_type
attributes.description: The methodology used to assign conversion credit across touchpoints. Last-click assigns 100% credit to the final touchpoint; first-click to the initial touchpoint; linear distributes credit equally; time-decay gives more weight to recent interactions; position-based (U-shaped) emphasizes first and last; algorithmic/data-driven uses machine learning to determine credit distribution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: last_click|first_click|linear|time_decay|position_based|algorithmic|data_driven — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the attribution model configuration (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1.3'). Incremented when model parameters, weighting rules, or conversion definitions are updated. Enables historical comparison and audit trail.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this attribution model record was last modified. Updated whenever any configuration parameter changes. Part of standard audit trail.

attributes.name: reporting_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code used for all revenue and ROI calculations in this attribution model (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP'). Ensures consistent financial reporting across campaigns.

products.name: conversion_event
products.description: Transactional record of a customer conversion event attributed to a marketing campaign or touchpoint. Captures conversion event type (purchase, sign-up, loyalty enrollment, app install, BOPIS order, email subscription, account creation), customer identifier, order or transaction reference, conversion timestamp, attributed campaign, attributed channel, attribution model applied, attributed revenue value, and conversion path length (number of touchpoints). Serves as the authoritative record linking marketing activity to business outcomes.

attributes.name: conversion_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the conversion event record. Primary key.

attributes.name: assisted_by_conversion_event_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on conversion_event (assisted_by_conversion_event_id)

attributes.name: attribution_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.attribution_model. Business justification: Conversion events are attributed using attribution models. The conversion_event table has attribution_model (STRING) which stores the model name, but this should be normalized to a FK to attribution_m

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the marketing campaign attributed to this conversion event. Links to the campaign that drove the conversion.

attributes.name: conversion_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that created this conversion event record. Audit trail for record origin.

attributes.name: conversion_modified_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this conversion event record. Audit trail for record changes.

attributes.name: header_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the order or transaction associated with this conversion event, if applicable. Null for non-purchase conversions.

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physical store associated with this conversion event, if applicable. Relevant for BOPIS (Buy Online Pick Up In Store) and in-store conversions.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the customer who completed the conversion event. Links to the customer who performed the action.

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.sku. Business justification: Conversion events must track which specific SKUs were purchased to attribute revenue to marketing activities at product level. Essential for product-level marketing attribution, calculating SKU-specif

attributes.name: storefront_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ecommerce.storefront. Business justification: Conversions happen on specific storefronts. Essential for multi-channel conversion tracking, storefront-level marketing ROI calculation, and channel performance comparison—core requirement for retaile

attributes.name: web_session_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the web or app session during which the conversion occurred. Links conversion to broader session analytics.

attributes.name: attributed_channel
attributes.description: Marketing channel attributed to driving this conversion event based on the attribution model applied. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: email|social_media|paid_search|organic_search|display|affiliate|direct — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: attributed_revenue_amount
attributes.description: Revenue value attributed to this conversion event in the base currency. Represents the monetary value generated by the conversion.

attributes.name: attributed_touchpoint
attributes.description: Specific marketing touchpoint or interaction attributed to driving this conversion. May include campaign creative, ad placement, or email message identifier.

attributes.name: browser
attributes.description: Web browser used by the customer at the time of conversion. Captured for technical and user experience analysis.

attributes.name: conversion_event_code
attributes.description: Business-readable unique code identifying this conversion event for reporting and tracking purposes.

attributes.name: conversion_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this conversion event. Captures additional context or special circumstances.

attributes.name: conversion_page_url
attributes.description: URL of the page where the conversion event was completed. Identifies the exact location of the conversion action.

attributes.name: conversion_path_length
attributes.description: Number of marketing touchpoints the customer interacted with before completing this conversion event. Measures the complexity of the customer journey.

attributes.name: conversion_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the conversion event. Tracks whether the conversion was successfully completed or encountered issues.

attributes.name: conversion_timestamp
attributes.description: Exact date and time when the conversion event occurred. Represents the moment the customer completed the conversion action.

attributes.name: conversion_type
attributes.description: Type of conversion event that occurred. Categorizes the nature of the customer action that constitutes a conversion.

attributes.name: conversion_value
attributes.description: Business value assigned to this conversion event, which may differ from revenue for non-purchase conversions. Used for ROI and campaign effectiveness measurement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this conversion event record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Type of device used by the customer when the conversion event occurred. Enables device-based conversion analysis.

attributes.name: geographic_city
attributes.description: City where the customer was located at the time of conversion. Supports city-level conversion tracking.

attributes.name: geographic_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the geographic location of the customer at the time of conversion.

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: State, province, or region where the customer was located at the time of conversion. Enables regional conversion analysis.

attributes.name: is_new_customer
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this conversion represents a new customer acquisition. True if this is the customers first conversion event.

attributes.name: is_omnichannel
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this conversion involved multiple channels in the customer journey. True if the conversion path crossed online and offline touchpoints.

attributes.name: landing_page_url
attributes.description: URL of the page where the customer first landed in the session that led to conversion. Entry point for the conversion journey.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this conversion event record was last modified. Audit trail for record updates.

attributes.name: operating_system
attributes.description: Operating system of the device used at the time of conversion. Supports platform-specific conversion analysis.

attributes.name: referrer_url
attributes.description: URL of the page that referred the customer to the conversion page. Captures the immediate source of traffic.

attributes.name: revenue_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the attributed revenue amount.

attributes.name: time_to_conversion_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours elapsed from the first attributed touchpoint to the conversion event. Measures the length of the conversion cycle.

attributes.name: utm_campaign
attributes.description: UTM campaign parameter captured at the time of conversion. Identifies the specific campaign that drove the conversion.

attributes.name: utm_content
attributes.description: UTM content parameter captured at the time of conversion. Differentiates similar content or links within the same campaign.

attributes.name: utm_medium
attributes.description: UTM medium parameter captured at the time of conversion. Identifies the marketing medium used.

attributes.name: utm_source
attributes.description: UTM source parameter captured at the time of conversion. Identifies the traffic source that referred the customer.

attributes.name: utm_term
attributes.description: UTM term parameter captured at the time of conversion. Identifies paid search keywords.

products.name: marketing_budget

attributes.name: marketing_budget_id

attributes.name: campaign_id

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Reference to the finance cost center responsible for this marketing budget allocation. Links to finance.cost_center for GL reconciliation.

attributes.name: finance_budget_id

attributes.name: marketing_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who created this budget record.

attributes.name: marketing_brand_id

attributes.name: marketing_modified_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who last modified this budget record.

attributes.name: primary_marketing_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or user who owns and is accountable for this budget allocation and its performance.

attributes.name: revised_from_marketing_budget_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on marketing_budget (revised_from_marketing_budget_id)

attributes.name: actual_spend_to_date
attributes.description: Total actual expenditure against this budget as of the current date, including all invoiced and paid amounts.

attributes.name: agency_fees_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for external agency retainers, project fees, and consulting services.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval workflow status for this budget allocation. Tracks progression through the approval chain.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this budget allocation was officially approved and became active.

attributes.name: budget_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code for the budget allocation, used for cross-system reference and reporting.

attributes.name: budget_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the marketing budget allocation (e.g., 'Q1 2024 Digital Campaign Budget', 'Holiday Season Omnichannel Budget').

attributes.name: budget_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the budget allocation. Tracks progression from draft through approval to active execution and closure.

attributes.name: committed_spend
attributes.description: Total amount of budget committed through media buys, agency contracts, and vendor bookings but not yet invoiced or paid.

attributes.name: content_production_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for creative content production including photography, videography, copywriting, and design services.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this budget record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget amounts (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: digital_channel_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation specifically for digital marketing channels including e-commerce, social media, search, display, and email.

attributes.name: display_advertising_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for display advertising including banner ads, video ads, and programmatic advertising.

attributes.name: email_marketing_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for email marketing campaigns, automation platforms, and SMS marketing activities.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Effective end date for this budget allocation period. Spending against this budget must occur before this date.

attributes.name: events_sponsorship_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for event marketing, trade shows, sponsorships, and experiential marketing activities.

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period within the year (quarterly, half-yearly, or annual) for which this budget is allocated. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|H1|H2|Annual — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this budget allocation applies (e.g., 2024).

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic scope of the marketing budget allocation indicating whether it covers national, regional, local, or international markets.

attributes.name: influencer_marketing_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for influencer partnerships, sponsored content, and brand ambassador programs.

attributes.name: last_revision_date
attributes.description: Date when this budget allocation was last revised or amended. Tracks budget reforecasting and reallocation activities.

attributes.name: market_research_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for market research, consumer insights, competitive analysis, and brand tracking studies.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this budget record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes and comments about this budget allocation including strategic context, constraints, or special instructions.

attributes.name: remaining_budget
attributes.description: Remaining unallocated budget calculated as total approved budget minus committed spend and actual spend to date.

attributes.name: revision_reason
attributes.description: Business justification or reason for the most recent budget revision (e.g., 'Increased holiday season demand', 'Campaign performance reallocation').

attributes.name: search_engine_marketing_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for paid search advertising including Google Ads, Bing Ads, and other search engine marketing platforms.

attributes.name: social_media_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation specifically for social media marketing activities across platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, TikTok).

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Effective start date for this budget allocation period. Spending against this budget is valid from this date forward.

attributes.name: target_country_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes where this budget will be deployed (e.g., 'USA,CAN,MEX').

attributes.name: target_revenue_goal
attributes.description: Target revenue goal that this marketing budget is expected to generate or influence through campaign activities.

attributes.name: target_roi_percentage
attributes.description: Target return on investment percentage expected from this marketing budget allocation. Used for performance measurement and attribution analysis.

attributes.name: total_approved_budget
attributes.description: Total approved budget amount for this allocation across all channels and campaigns. Represents the authorized spending limit.

attributes.name: traditional_channel_budget
attributes.description: Budget allocation for traditional marketing channels including TV, radio, print, outdoor, and direct mail.

attributes.name: utilization_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of total approved budget that has been spent or committed, calculated as (actual_spend_to_date + committed_spend) / total_approved_budget * 100.
