attributes.name: channel_type
attributes.description: Specific type of marketing channel. Examples: email, SMS (Short Message Service), push notification, paid search, paid social, display advertising, video, OOH (Out-of-Home), print, radio, TV (Television), in-store, affiliate. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: email|sms|push|paid_search|paid_social|display|video|ooh|print|radio|tv|in_store|affiliate — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: channel_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the channel for reporting and integration purposes.

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Notes on regulatory compliance requirements specific to this channel (e.g., CAN-SPAM for email, TCPA for SMS, GDPR for digital advertising in EU).

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: End date or renewal date of the vendor contract for this channel. Null if contract is evergreen or month-to-month.

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the vendor contract or service agreement for this channel.

attributes.name: cost_model
attributes.description: Pricing model for the channel: CPM (Cost Per Mille/Thousand Impressions), CPC (Cost Per Click), CPA (Cost Per Acquisition), flat (fixed fee), hybrid (combination), performance (outcome-based).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this channel record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all cost metrics associated with this channel (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: data_refresh_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which performance data from this channel is refreshed in the marketing analytics platform: real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, or manual.

attributes.name: channel_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the channel, including its purpose, audience reach, and typical use cases within the marketing strategy.

attributes.name: geographic_coverage
attributes.description: Geographic regions or markets where this channel is available and effective (e.g., USA, CAN, GBR, global).

attributes.name: integration_status
attributes.description: Current integration status with the marketing automation platform: integrated (fully connected), pending (in progress), not_integrated (manual or offline), deprecated (legacy, no longer used).

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether the channel is currently active and available for campaign execution. True if active, False if inactive or retired.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this channel record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: channel_name
attributes.description: The business name of the marketing channel (e.g., Google Ads, Facebook, Email Newsletter, In-Store Display).

attributes.name: owner_email
attributes.description: Email address of the channel owner for operational communication and escalation.

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or team responsible for managing and optimizing this channel.

attributes.name: platform_vendor_name
attributes.description: Name of the platform or vendor providing the channel service (e.g., Google, Meta, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Mailchimp, Adobe Campaign).

attributes.name: primary_kpi
attributes.description: The primary key performance indicator used to measure success for this channel (e.g., CTR (Click-Through Rate), conversion rate, ROAS (Return on Ad Spend), engagement rate).

attributes.name: supports_ab_testing
attributes.description: Indicates whether the channel supports A/B testing or multivariate testing for campaign optimization. True if supported, False otherwise.

attributes.name: supports_automation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the channel supports marketing automation workflows (e.g., triggered campaigns, drip sequences). True if supported, False otherwise.

attributes.name: supports_personalization
attributes.description: Indicates whether the channel supports personalized content delivery based on customer data and segmentation. True if supported, False otherwise.

attributes.name: target_audience_profile
attributes.description: Description of the typical audience demographics and psychographics that this channel reaches most effectively.

attributes.name: vendor_contract_number
attributes.description: Contract or agreement number with the channel vendor or platform provider, used for procurement and compliance tracking.

products.name: utm_parameter
products.description: Master record for standardized UTM parameter configurations used to tag marketing URLs for campaign tracking across digital channels. Captures UTM source, UTM medium, UTM campaign, UTM content, UTM term, full tagged URL, campaign reference, channel reference, creative asset reference, creation date, created by, and active status. Ensures consistent UTM taxonomy governance to prevent fragmented or inconsistent tagging that would corrupt attribution and web analytics data.

attributes.name: utm_parameter_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the UTM parameter configuration record.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent marketing campaign that this UTM parameter configuration supports.

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.marketing_channel. Business justification: UTM parameters are used to tag URLs for channel tracking and should reference the authoritative marketing_channel master. Currently, utm_parameter has a denormalized channel_type STRING attribute. Add

attributes.name: derived_from_utm_parameter_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on utm_parameter (derived_from_utm_parameter_id)

attributes.name: primary_utm_associate_id
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who created this UTM parameter configuration record.

attributes.name: tertiary_utm_approved_by_user_associate_id
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who approved this UTM parameter configuration for campaign use.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this UTM parameter configuration was approved for use in marketing campaigns.

attributes.name: base_url
attributes.description: The destination URL before UTM parameters are appended (e.g., https://www.retailer.com/products/shoes). Used as the foundation for tagged URL construction.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this UTM parameter configuration record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: creative_asset_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the creative asset (banner, video, email template) associated with this UTM configuration. Links to Digital Asset Management (DAM) system.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date after which this UTM parameter configuration is no longer valid for use. Null indicates no expiration.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this UTM parameter configuration is valid and approved for use in marketing campaigns.

attributes.name: full_tagged_url
attributes.description: Complete URL with all UTM parameters appended as query string. This is the final URL used in marketing materials and campaigns.

attributes.name: geographic_target
attributes.description: Geographic scope for this UTM configuration (e.g., USA, CAN, GBR, global). Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or 'global' for worldwide campaigns.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this UTM parameter configuration is currently active and approved for use in marketing campaigns.

attributes.name: last_used_date
attributes.description: Date when this UTM parameter configuration was most recently used in a campaign or marketing material.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this UTM parameter configuration record was most recently modified.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, usage instructions, or special considerations for this UTM parameter configuration.

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: Name of the marketing team or business unit responsible for managing and maintaining this UTM parameter configuration.

attributes.name: parameter_code
attributes.description: Unique business code for this UTM parameter configuration, used for system integration and lookup.

attributes.name: parameter_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name for this UTM parameter configuration, used for internal reference and governance.

attributes.name: parameter_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this UTM parameter configuration. Active configurations are approved for use in campaigns.

attributes.name: platform_integration
attributes.description: Name of the marketing platform or tool where this UTM configuration is deployed (e.g., Google Ads, Facebook Ads Manager, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Mailchimp).

attributes.name: short_url
attributes.description: Shortened version of the full tagged URL, used in space-constrained marketing materials such as SMS, social media posts, or print ads.

attributes.name: target_audience_segment
attributes.description: Description of the audience segment this UTM configuration is intended to reach (e.g., high_value_customers, new_prospects, cart_abandoners).

attributes.name: taxonomy_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the UTM taxonomy standard applied to this configuration. Ensures consistency across campaigns and prevents taxonomy drift.

attributes.name: tracking_domain
attributes.description: Domain used for URL shortening or click tracking (e.g., bit.ly, custom branded domain). Used when the full tagged URL is shortened for display purposes.

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Number of times this UTM parameter configuration has been deployed in marketing campaigns or materials. Used for governance and reuse tracking.

attributes.name: utm_campaign
attributes.description: Identifies the specific campaign name (e.g., spring_sale_2024, black_friday, back_to_school). Used to group related marketing efforts.

attributes.name: utm_content
attributes.description: Identifies the specific content or creative variant within a campaign (e.g., banner_ad_1, text_link, hero_image). Used for A/B testing and creative performance analysis.

attributes.name: utm_medium
attributes.description: Identifies the marketing medium (e.g., cpc, email, social, display, affiliate). Represents the channel type.

attributes.name: utm_source
attributes.description: Identifies the source of traffic (e.g., google, facebook, newsletter, affiliate_partner). Represents the referrer or origin platform.

attributes.name: utm_term
attributes.description: Identifies the paid search keyword or term that triggered the ad (e.g., running_shoes, discount_electronics). Primarily used for paid search campaigns.

attributes.name: validation_errors
attributes.description: Description of any validation errors or warnings identified during automated quality checks. Used for governance and correction workflows.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of automated validation checks for this UTM parameter configuration. Ensures compliance with naming conventions and taxonomy rules.

products.name: ab_test_campaign
products.description: Master record for A/B and multivariate tests conducted within marketing campaigns to optimize creative, messaging, audience targeting, and channel strategy. Captures test name, campaign reference, test type (subject line, creative variant, send time, audience split, channel mix), hypothesis, control and variant definitions, audience split percentages, test start/end dates, primary success metric, statistical significance threshold, winning variant, and test status. Distinct from ecommerce.ab_test which governs on-site UX experiments — this entity governs marketing message and channel experiments.

attributes.name: ab_test_campaign_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the A/B test campaign record. Primary key.

attributes.name: ab_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or user who created this A/B test campaign record.

attributes.name: ab_modified_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or user who last modified this A/B test campaign record.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the audience segment used for this A/B test, defining the target population.

attributes.name: baseline_ab_test_campaign_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on ab_test_campaign (baseline_ab_test_campaign_id)

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent marketing campaign under which this A/B test is conducted.

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.marketing_channel. Business justification: A/B test campaigns are conducted within specific marketing channels and should reference the authoritative marketing_channel master. Currently, ab_test_campaign has a denormalized channel_tested STRIN

attributes.name: creative_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.creative_asset. Business justification: A/B tests often test different creative variants. The ab_test_campaign should link to the creative_asset being tested. The control_variant_definition and test_variant_definition are STRING description

attributes.name: primary_ab_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or user responsible for designing, executing, and analyzing this A/B test.

attributes.name: test_sku_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.sku_price. Business justification: A/B tests in retail frequently test different price points or promotional depths. Test variant definitions require linking to the specific prices being tested. Real business process: promotional optim

attributes.name: actual_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when the A/B test campaign execution ended.

attributes.name: actual_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when the A/B test campaign execution began.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the A/B test design and execution plan has been approved by the appropriate stakeholders.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the A/B test campaign was approved for execution.

attributes.name: confidence_level_pct
attributes.description: The actual confidence level achieved in the test results, indicating the statistical reliability of the outcome.

attributes.name: control_audience_size
attributes.description: Number of individuals or contacts assigned to the control variant.

attributes.name: control_audience_split_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the total audience allocated to the control variant (e.g., 50.00 for a 50/50 split).

attributes.name: control_metric_value
attributes.description: The measured value of the primary success metric for the control variant (e.g., 25.50 for 25.5% open rate).

attributes.name: control_variant_definition
attributes.description: Detailed description of the control (baseline) variant used in the test, including creative elements, messaging, and configuration.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this A/B test campaign record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: hypothesis
attributes.description: The hypothesis statement describing the expected outcome or behavior change being tested (e.g., 'Changing subject line to include urgency will increase open rate by 10%').

attributes.name: lift_pct
attributes.description: The percentage improvement (or decline) of the test variant over the control variant for the primary success metric.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this A/B test campaign record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: primary_success_metric
attributes.description: The key performance indicator (KPI) used to determine the winning variant (e.g., open rate, click-through rate, conversion rate, revenue, engagement rate).

attributes.name: statistical_significance_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The confidence level threshold (e.g., 95.00) required to declare a variant as statistically significant winner.

attributes.name: test_audience_size
attributes.description: Number of individuals or contacts assigned to the test variant(s).

attributes.name: test_audience_split_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the total audience allocated to the test variant(s) (e.g., 50.00 for a 50/50 split).

attributes.name: test_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code assigned to the test for tracking and reference across systems.

attributes.name: test_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the A/B test objectives, methodology, and expected business impact.

attributes.name: test_end_date
attributes.description: The date when the A/B test campaign concluded or is scheduled to conclude.

attributes.name: test_metric_value
attributes.description: The measured value of the primary success metric for the test variant (e.g., 28.75 for 28.75% open rate).

attributes.name: test_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the A/B or multivariate test for identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: test_notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, observations, or learnings captured during or after the test execution.

attributes.name: test_start_date
attributes.description: The date when the A/B test campaign was launched and began collecting data.

attributes.name: test_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the A/B test campaign (draft, scheduled, running, completed, cancelled, paused).

attributes.name: test_type
attributes.description: Category of the test indicating what element is being tested (e.g., subject line, creative variant, send time, audience split, channel mix, landing page).

attributes.name: test_variant_definition
attributes.description: Detailed description of the test (challenger) variant(s) used in the experiment, including creative elements, messaging, and configuration.

attributes.name: total_audience_size
attributes.description: Total number of individuals or contacts included in the A/B test across all variants.

attributes.name: winning_variant
attributes.description: Indicates which variant won the test based on the primary success metric (control, test, or inconclusive if no clear winner).

products.name: automation_flow
products.description: Master record for marketing automation journeys and triggered workflow programs configured in the marketing automation platform (e.g., Salesforce Marketing Cloud Journey Builder, Braze Canvas, Klaviyo Flow). Captures flow name, trigger event (cart abandonment, loyalty enrollment, birthday, win-back, post-purchase, browse abandonment), channel sequence (email → SMS → push), entry criteria, exit criteria, wait periods, branching logic description, campaign association, active status, and total enrolled count.

attributes.name: automation_flow_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the marketing automation flow or journey program. Primary key.

attributes.name: automation_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the marketing team member or user responsible for managing and optimizing this automation flow.

attributes.name: automation_created_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who originally created this automation flow configuration. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

attributes.name: automation_modified_by_associate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the user who last modified this automation flow configuration. Tracks change ownership for governance.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent marketing campaign that this automation flow supports. Links the flow to broader campaign strategy and budget.

attributes.name: cloned_from_automation_flow_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on automation_flow (cloned_from_automation_flow_id)

attributes.name: target_audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer segment that is eligible for this automation flow. Defines the population scope for enrollment.

attributes.name: activation_date
attributes.description: Date when the automation flow was first activated and began enrolling customers. Marks the start of the flows operational lifecycle.

attributes.name: active_enrolled_count
attributes.description: Current number of customers actively progressing through the flow (not yet completed or exited). Indicates in-flight journey volume.

attributes.name: branching_logic_description
attributes.description: Description of conditional branching and decision points within the flow (e.g., 'If email opened, send offer; if not opened after 24h, send reminder'). Captures personalization and dynamic path logic.

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: The business unit, brand, or division that owns this automation flow (e.g., 'Grocery', 'Apparel', 'Electronics'). Used for organizational segmentation and reporting.

attributes.name: channel_sequence
attributes.description: Ordered list of marketing channels used in this flow (e.g., 'email → SMS → push notification', 'email → email → SMS'). Describes the multi-touch communication strategy.

attributes.name: completed_count
attributes.description: Total number of customers who have completed all steps in the automation flow. Measures journey completion rate.

attributes.name: consent_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether explicit customer consent is required before enrollment in this flow. Critical for General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this automation flow record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and governance.

attributes.name: deactivation_date
attributes.description: Date when the automation flow was deactivated or paused, stopping new customer enrollments. Null if the flow is still active.

attributes.name: entry_criteria
attributes.description: Detailed business rules and conditions that a customer must meet to enter this automation flow. May include segment membership, purchase history, engagement thresholds, or attribute filters.

attributes.name: exit_criteria
attributes.description: Conditions under which a customer is removed from the automation flow before completion (e.g., purchase made, unsubscribed, goal achieved, maximum time elapsed).

attributes.name: flow_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code for the automation flow, used for external reference and integration with marketing automation platforms.

attributes.name: flow_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the automation flows purpose, strategy, and expected customer experience. Provides context for stakeholders and future reference.

attributes.name: flow_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the marketing automation flow or journey (e.g., 'Cart Abandonment Recovery', 'Loyalty Welcome Series', 'Post-Purchase Thank You').

attributes.name: flow_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the automation flow: draft (being configured), active (running and enrolling customers), paused (temporarily stopped), completed (finished execution), or archived (historical record).

attributes.name: flow_type
attributes.description: Classification of the automation flow based on execution pattern: triggered by customer action, scheduled at specific times, recurring on a cadence, one-time campaign, event-based, or behavioral targeting.

attributes.name: goal_achieved_count
attributes.description: Number of customers who achieved the defined goal while enrolled in this flow. Primary success metric for conversion attribution.

attributes.name: goal_definition
attributes.description: The primary business objective or conversion goal for this automation flow (e.g., 'Complete purchase', 'Activate loyalty account', 'Re-engage dormant customer', 'Increase Average Order Value (AOV)').

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this automation flow record was last modified. Tracks configuration changes and updates over time.

attributes.name: planned_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the automation flow to conclude or be archived. Used for time-bound campaigns or seasonal flows.

attributes.name: platform_flow_code
attributes.description: External identifier for this flow in the source marketing automation platform. Used for integration and reconciliation with platform reporting.

attributes.name: platform_name
attributes.description: Name of the marketing automation platform where this flow is configured (e.g., 'Salesforce Marketing Cloud', 'Braze', 'Klaviyo', 'Adobe Campaign', 'HubSpot').

attributes.name: primary_channel
attributes.description: The main marketing channel used for this automation flow. Determines platform integration and message delivery infrastructure.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to this automation flow, indicating its strategic importance and resource allocation precedence.

attributes.name: step_count
attributes.description: Total number of steps or touchpoints configured in this automation flow. Indicates complexity and length of the customer journey.

attributes.name: suppression_list_applied_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether suppression lists (unsubscribed, opted-out, or blocked customers) are enforced for this flow to ensure compliance with communication preferences.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of tags or labels applied to this flow for categorization, search, and reporting (e.g., 'retention', 'seasonal', 'high-value', 'mobile-first').

attributes.name: test_mode_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this flow is running in test or preview mode (not sending to real customers). Used during configuration and quality assurance.

attributes.name: total_enrolled_count
attributes.description: Cumulative number of customers who have entered this automation flow since activation. Key metric for reach and scale assessment.

attributes.name: trigger_event
attributes.description: The specific customer behavior or system event that initiates entry into this automation flow (e.g., 'cart_abandonment', 'loyalty_enrollment', 'birthday', 'win_back', 'post_purchase', 'browse_abandonment', 'product_back_in_stock').

attributes.name: wait_period_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of wait times and delays between steps in the flow (e.g., 'Wait 2 hours, then wait 1 day, then wait 3 days'). Defines the timing cadence of the journey.

products.name: automation_enrollment
products.description: Transactional record capturing each customer's entry into and progression through a marketing automation flow. Captures customer identifier, automation flow reference, enrollment trigger event, enrollment timestamp, current step in the flow, step history, exit reason (completed, unsubscribed, suppressed, manually removed), exit timestamp, and conversion flag. Enables operational monitoring of automation flow health and customer journey progression.

attributes.name: automation_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the automation enrollment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: audience_segment_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the audience segment that the customer belonged to at the time of enrollment. Used for targeting analysis and segment performance measurement.

attributes.name: automation_flow_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the marketing automation flow that the customer was enrolled into. References the specific automation campaign or journey definition.

attributes.name: automation_step_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the current step or stage in the automation flow where the customer is positioned. Null if the customer has exited the flow.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent marketing campaign that this automation enrollment is associated with. Links the automation flow to broader campaign strategy and budget.

attributes.name: primary_automation_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that created this enrollment record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the customer enrolled in the automation flow. Links to the customer who entered the marketing automation journey.

attributes.name: re_enrolled_from_automation_enrollment_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Re Enrolled From Automation Enrollment Id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on automation_enrollment (re_enrolled_from_automation_enrollment_id)

tag_set.value: Re Enrolled From Automation Enrollment Id

attributes.name: consent_status
attributes.description: The current consent status of the customer for receiving marketing communications in this automation flow. Ensures compliance with data privacy regulations.

attributes.name: conversion_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the conversion value amount.

attributes.name: conversion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer achieved the target conversion goal of the automation flow. True if the customer completed the desired action (purchase, sign-up, engagement), false otherwise.

attributes.name: conversion_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the customer achieved the conversion goal. Null if no conversion occurred.

attributes.name: conversion_value_amount
attributes.description: The monetary value attributed to the conversion event. Represents revenue, order value, or estimated customer lifetime value (CLTV) impact from the automation-driven conversion.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this enrollment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: current_step_entry_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the customer entered the current step of the automation flow. Used to calculate time-in-step and identify stalled journeys.

attributes.name: enrollment_channel
attributes.description: The primary marketing channel through which the automation flow communicates with the customer. Indicates the delivery mechanism for automation messages.

attributes.name: enrollment_code
attributes.description: Business-readable unique code for this enrollment instance. Used for operational tracking and customer service reference.

attributes.name: enrollment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this enrollment. Used for operational context, troubleshooting, or manual intervention documentation.

attributes.name: enrollment_source
attributes.description: The system or method that initiated the enrollment. Indicates whether the enrollment was triggered automatically by an event, manually by a user, or via batch processing.

attributes.name: enrollment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the customer within the automation flow. Indicates whether the customer is actively progressing, has completed, or has exited the flow.

attributes.name: enrollment_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the customer was enrolled into the automation flow. Represents the start of the customers journey through the automation.

attributes.name: enrollment_trigger_event
attributes.description: The business event or action that triggered the customers enrollment into the automation flow. Examples include cart abandonment, product purchase, account creation, loyalty tier change, or manual enrollment.

attributes.name: exit_reason
attributes.description: The reason the customer exited the automation flow. Examples include completed (finished all steps), unsubscribed (opted out), suppressed (consent withdrawn), manually_removed (admin action), goal_achieved (converted), or error (technical failure). Null if still active.

attributes.name: exit_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the customer exited the automation flow. Null if the customer is still actively enrolled.

attributes.name: last_interaction_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time of the customers most recent interaction with any message in this automation flow. Includes opens, clicks, or other engagement actions.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this enrollment record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: next_scheduled_action_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the next automation action (message send, step transition, or evaluation) is scheduled for this enrollment. Used for operational monitoring and queue management.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: The business priority assigned to this enrollment. High-priority enrollments may receive expedited processing or preferential treatment in message queues.

attributes.name: step_sequence_number
attributes.description: The ordinal position of the current step within the automation flow. Indicates progression depth through the journey.

attributes.name: suppression_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer is currently suppressed from receiving further messages in this automation flow due to consent withdrawal, unsubscribe, or compliance requirements.

attributes.name: suppression_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the customer was suppressed from the automation flow. Null if not suppressed.

attributes.name: total_messages_clicked
attributes.description: Count of marketing messages where the customer clicked a link or call-to-action during this automation enrollment. Indicates deeper engagement and intent.

attributes.name: total_messages_opened
attributes.description: Count of marketing messages that the customer opened during this automation enrollment. Used to measure engagement and message effectiveness.

attributes.name: total_messages_sent
attributes.description: Count of marketing messages (emails, SMS, push notifications) sent to the customer as part of this automation enrollment. Used to measure communication volume and frequency.

attributes.name: total_steps_completed
attributes.description: Count of automation flow steps that the customer has successfully completed since enrollment. Used to measure journey progression and engagement.

products.name: opt_in_record
products.description: Authoritative record of customer marketing communication opt-in and opt-out preferences by channel, distinct from customer.consent which covers broader GDPR/CCPA privacy consent. Captures customer identifier, channel type (email, SMS, push, direct mail, phone), opt-in status, opt-in source (checkout, loyalty enrollment, website preference center, in-store), opt-in timestamp, opt-out timestamp, opt-out reason, suppression list membership, and CAN-SPAM/TCPA compliance flags. Governs which customers can be contacted via each marketing channel.

attributes.name: opt_in_record_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the marketing communication opt-in record. Primary key for the opt-in record entity.

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to marketing.marketing_channel. Business justification: Opt-in records are channel-specific (email opt-in, SMS opt-in, push opt-in) and should reference the authoritative marketing_channel master. Currently, opt_in_record has a denormalized channel_type ST

attributes.name: opt_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that created this opt-in record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: opt_modified_by_user_associate_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system process that last modified this opt-in record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer who owns this opt-in preference. Links to the customer master record.

products.name: campaign_deployment
products.description: This association product represents the deployment of a marketing campaign to a specific digital storefront. It captures the operational execution of campaign strategy at the storefront level, including budget allocation, activation timing, and performance metrics specific to each campaign-storefront combination. Each record links one campaign to one storefront with attributes that exist only in the context of this deployment relationship.. Existence Justification: In retail operations, marketing campaigns are routinely deployed across multiple digital storefronts simultaneously (e.g., a national holiday campaign runs on the main e-commerce site, mobile app, and marketplace storefronts), and each storefront hosts multiple campaigns concurrently (seasonal promotions, category-specific campaigns, brand campaigns). Marketing teams actively manage these deployments as distinct operational entities, allocating budgets, setting activation windows, and tracking performance metrics at the campaign-storefront level.

products.name: campaign_fulfillment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment between marketing campaigns and distribution center facilities that fulfill campaign-driven demand. It captures the multi-facility fulfillment strategy for national and regional campaigns, where each DC is allocated specific inventory quantities, assigned priority rankings, and bound by campaign-specific SLAs. Each record links one campaign to one DC facility with attributes that exist only in the context of this fulfillment relationship.. Existence Justification: In retail operations, national and regional marketing campaigns are routinely fulfilled from multiple distribution centers based on geographic coverage, inventory positioning, and capacity. Each campaign-to-DC assignment is an operational decision with specific allocated inventory quantities, priority rankings for order routing, and campaign-specific fulfillment SLAs. Conversely, each DC simultaneously supports multiple active campaigns with different inventory allocations and priorities. This is an actively managed operational relationship, not a derived analytical correlation.

products.name: campaign_policy_compliance
products.description: This association product represents the compliance verification relationship between marketing campaigns and internal compliance policies. It captures the acknowledgment, verification, and exception management for each campaign-policy pairing. Each record links one campaign to one policy with attributes that track when compliance was verified, by whom, and whether any exceptions were granted.. Existence Justification: In retail operations, marketing campaigns must comply with multiple internal policies (data privacy, advertising standards, promotional terms, sweepstakes regulations, PCI security for payment promotions). Each policy applies to many campaigns across different brands, channels, and time periods. The compliance team actively manages campaign-policy compliance records as operational entities, tracking acknowledgment dates, verification status, reviewer assignments, and exception approvals for audit and regulatory reporting purposes.

Captures dimension name (store, channel, category, brand, region, time period, customer segment), dimension type (conformed, degenerate, role-playing), grain description, associated domain, hierarchy levels, and default sort order. Serves as the dimensional modeling backbone for OLAP cube design and BI tool semantic layer configuration.

attributes.name: metric_dimension_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the metric dimension master record. Primary key for the dimensional modeling backbone used in OLAP cube design and BI semantic layer configuration.

attributes.name: parent_metric_dimension_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on metric_dimension (parent_metric_dimension_id)

attributes.name: primary_replacement_metric_dimension_id
attributes.description: Reference to the metric_dimension_id of the dimension that replaces this deprecated dimension. Null if no replacement exists. Supports migration planning and backward compatibility mapping.

attributes.name: associated_domain
attributes.description: The primary data domain to which this dimension belongs, such as Customer, Product, Inventory, Order, Store, Supply Chain, Pricing, Promotion, or Finance. Aligns the dimension with enterprise data governance and domain ownership structures.

attributes.name: business_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the business unit, role, or individual responsible for the business definition, quality, and governance of this dimension. Typically a domain data steward or business subject matter expert.

attributes.name: business_rules
attributes.description: Documentation of business rules, constraints, and logic applied to this dimension. Examples include how dimension members are classified, how hierarchies are constructed, or how slowly changing dimension logic is applied.

attributes.name: cardinality_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated number of distinct members or rows in this dimension. Used for query optimization, index design, and OLAP cube sizing. For example, Store dimension might have 5000 members, while Time dimension at day grain might have 3650 members for 10 years.

attributes.name: compliance_tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of regulatory compliance frameworks or requirements applicable to this dimension. Examples include GDPR, CCPA, PCI DSS, SOX, HIPAA. Used for compliance reporting and audit trail documentation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dimension master record was first created in the semantic layer metadata repository. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_quality_rules
attributes.description: Specification of data quality rules and validation checks applied to this dimension. Includes completeness checks, uniqueness constraints, referential integrity rules, and acceptable value ranges.

attributes.name: default_aggregation
attributes.description: The default aggregation method to apply when this dimension is used in calculations or rolled up in hierarchies. Typically 'none' for true dimensions, but may specify aggregation for degenerate dimensions or dimension attributes used in calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sum|average|count|min|max|distinct_count|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: default_sort_order
attributes.description: Numeric value indicating the default display order of this dimension in BI tools, dashboards, and reports. Lower values appear first. Used to standardize dimension presentation across the enterprise semantic layer.

attributes.name: deprecated_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dimension has been deprecated and is scheduled for retirement. Deprecated dimensions should not be used in new reports or dashboards but are retained for backward compatibility.

attributes.name: deprecation_date
attributes.description: The date on which this dimension was marked as deprecated. Null if the dimension is not deprecated. Used for planning migration and retirement activities.

attributes.name: dimension_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code or abbreviation for the dimension, used as a technical identifier in BI tools and semantic layer configurations. Typically uppercase and concise for system integration.

attributes.name: dimension_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive business description of the dimension, its purpose, and how it should be used in analytics and reporting. Provides context for business users and data analysts consuming the semantic layer.

attributes.name: dimension_name
attributes.description: The business name of the dimension used to slice and filter KPIs and metrics in the retail semantic layer. Examples include Store, Channel, Category, Brand, Region, Time Period, Customer Segment.

attributes.name: dimension_type
attributes.description: Classification of the dimension based on dimensional modeling patterns. Conformed dimensions are shared across multiple fact tables; degenerate dimensions are stored in the fact table; role-playing dimensions serve multiple contexts; junk dimensions combine low-cardinality flags; slowly changing dimensions track historical changes; outrigger dimensions are secondary dimensions referenced by a primary dimension.

attributes.name: display_format
attributes.description: Specification of how dimension members should be formatted for display in BI tools and reports. Examples include date formats, number formats, or custom display templates for composite keys.

attributes.name: drill_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether drill-down and drill-up operations are enabled for this dimension in OLAP cubes and BI tools. Requires hierarchy_levels to be defined.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this dimension definition ceased to be effective. Null if the dimension is currently active. Used for historical tracking and version management of dimension metadata.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this dimension definition became effective and available for use in the semantic layer. Supports temporal validity and version control of dimension metadata.

attributes.name: filter_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dimension is available for use as a filter in BI tools and dashboards. Some dimensions may be display-only and not suitable for filtering due to cardinality or performance considerations.

attributes.name: grain_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the level of detail or granularity represented by this dimension. Defines what one row in the dimension table represents, such as individual store location, daily time period, or product SKU level.

attributes.name: hierarchy_levels
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of hierarchical levels within the dimension, ordered from most granular to most aggregated. For example, Store dimension might have: Store > District > Region > Division. Time dimension might have: Day > Week > Month > Quarter > Year. Supports drill-down and roll-up analytics.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dimension is currently active and available for use in BI tools, semantic layers, and OLAP cubes. Inactive dimensions are retained for historical reference but not exposed to end users.

attributes.name: is_conformed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dimension is a conformed dimension shared across multiple fact tables and business processes. Conformed dimensions enable consistent cross-process reporting and are a cornerstone of enterprise data warehouse design.

attributes.name: is_slowly_changing
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dimension tracks historical changes over time using Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) techniques. True if the dimension maintains history of attribute changes; false if only current state is maintained.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this dimension master record was last updated. Tracks the most recent change to dimension metadata, supporting change management and audit requirements.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional notes, comments, or documentation about this dimension. Used for capturing implementation details, known issues, or special handling instructions.

attributes.name: refresh_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which this dimension is refreshed from source systems. Determines data latency and impacts BI tool cache strategies and OLAP cube processing schedules.

attributes.name: scd_type
attributes.description: Classification of the SCD technique applied to this dimension. Type 0: retain original; Type 1: overwrite; Type 2: add new row with versioning; Type 3: add new column; Type 4: separate history table; Type 6: hybrid (1+2+3). Not applicable if is_slowly_changing is false. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: type_0|type_1|type_2|type_3|type_4|type_6|not_applicable — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: security_classification
attributes.description: Data classification level for this dimension, determining access controls and data handling requirements. Public: no restrictions; Internal: company employees only; Confidential: sensitive business data; Restricted: highly sensitive data requiring special authorization.

attributes.name: technical_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the technical team, role, or individual responsible for the implementation, maintenance, and technical quality of this dimension in the semantic layer and BI platforms.

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Number of fact tables, KPIs, metrics, dashboards, or reports that reference this dimension. High usage count indicates a critical conformed dimension; low usage may indicate a candidate for deprecation or consolidation.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this dimension definition. Incremented when significant changes are made to dimension structure, hierarchy, or business rules. Supports change management and impact analysis.

products.name: dq_rule

Captures rule name, rule type (completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, timeliness, referential integrity), target domain and product, SQL or expression-based rule logic, severity level (critical, major, minor), expected threshold, remediation owner, and rule status. Serves as the authoritative registry of all DQ controls enforced in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: dq_rule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the data quality rule. Primary key for the DQ rule registry.

attributes.name: compliance_program_id

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User ID of the data steward or governance authority who approved this rule for production use. Required for critical and major severity rules.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rule was formally approved for enforcement. Null for draft or unapproved rules.

attributes.name: blocking_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether violations of this rule should halt downstream pipeline execution. True for critical data integrity rules; false for monitoring-only rules.

attributes.name: business_justification
attributes.description: Explanation of the business need or regulatory requirement driving this rule. Links rule to business outcomes, compliance mandates, or risk mitigation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rule record was first created in the registry. Immutable audit field.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: Link to detailed documentation, runbook, or knowledge base article explaining this rule, its business context, and remediation procedures.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date when this rule version became active and began enforcement. Used for temporal rule versioning and audit trail.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date when this rule version was superseded or retired. Null for currently active rules. Supports rule history and compliance audits.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: Cadence at which this rule is evaluated. Real-time rules run on every record insert/update; batch rules run on scheduled intervals.

attributes.name: execution_layer
attributes.description: Lakehouse medallion layer where this rule is enforced. Bronze for ingestion validation, Silver for transformation quality, Gold for consumption readiness.

attributes.name: last_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this rule was most recently evaluated. Used to monitor rule execution health and detect stale rules.

attributes.name: last_violation_count
attributes.description: Number of records that failed this rule during the most recent execution. Used for trend analysis and alerting.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or service account that last updated this rule definition. Used for change tracking and accountability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the most recent update to this rule record. Updated on every change for audit trail.

attributes.name: notification_enabled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether automated alerts should be sent when this rule is violated. True enables email/Slack/PagerDuty notifications.

attributes.name: notification_recipients
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses, Slack channels, or distribution lists to notify when this rule is violated. Used by alerting engine.

attributes.name: quarantine_enabled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether records violating this rule should be moved to a quarantine table for manual review. True enables automatic quarantine workflow.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation of applicable regulation, standard, or policy requiring this rule (e.g., GDPR Article 5, SOX Section 404, PCI DSS 3.2). Null if rule is business-driven only.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Prescribed corrective action or workflow to be triggered when this rule is violated. May reference automated fix procedures or manual investigation steps.

attributes.name: remediation_owner
attributes.description: Business role, team, or individual responsible for investigating and resolving violations of this rule. Used for incident routing and accountability.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or mnemonic code for the rule. Used for cross-system reference and automation.

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Detailed business explanation of what the rule validates, why it matters, and what constitutes a violation. Used for documentation and training.

attributes.name: rule_logic
attributes.description: SQL expression, Python function, or declarative logic defining the rule condition. Returns true for valid records, false for violations.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the data quality rule. Used for identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: rule_priority
attributes.description: Execution order priority when multiple rules apply to the same target. Lower numbers execute first. Used to sequence dependent validations.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rule. Active rules are enforced in production; inactive/deprecated rules are retained for audit history.

attributes.name: rule_tags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of metadata tags for rule categorization and filtering (e.g., PII, financial, regulatory, master_data). Used for rule discovery and reporting.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Category of data quality dimension this rule enforces: completeness (null checks), uniqueness (duplicate detection), validity (format/range checks), consistency (cross-field logic), timeliness (freshness checks), or referential integrity (FK validation).

attributes.name: rule_version
attributes.description: Semantic version identifier for this rule definition (e.g., 1.0.0, 2.1.3). Incremented when rule logic, thresholds, or scope change.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Business impact classification of rule violations. Critical violations block downstream processing; warnings are logged but do not halt pipelines.

attributes.name: target_attribute
attributes.description: The specific column or attribute within the target product that this rule validates. Null if rule applies to entire product or multiple attributes.

attributes.name: target_domain
attributes.description: The business domain (e.g., Customer, Product, Order, Inventory) to which this rule applies. Aligns with enterprise data domain taxonomy.

attributes.name: target_product
attributes.description: The specific data product or table within the target domain that this rule validates. Fully qualified name in domain.product format.

attributes.name: threshold_operator
attributes.description: Comparison operator applied to threshold_value. Defines whether the measured metric must be above, below, or equal to the threshold.

attributes.name: threshold_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for threshold_value. Percentage for error rates, count for absolute violations, ratio for proportional checks.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold for rule pass/fail determination. Interpretation depends on threshold_operator (e.g., error rate must be less than 0.05).

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or service account that originally defined this rule. Used for accountability and change tracking.

products.name: dq_result
products.description: Transactional record capturing the outcome of a data quality rule execution against a target data product. Stores rule execution timestamp, target domain, target product, records evaluated count, records failed count, failure rate, pass/fail status, sample failed record keys, and remediation action taken. Enables DQ trend monitoring, SLA compliance tracking, and data trust scoring across the retail lakehouse.

attributes.name: batch_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch or job that executed this rule. Used to group multiple rule executions that ran together as part of a scheduled DQ assessment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DQ result record was first created in the lakehouse. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_snapshot_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the data snapshot that was evaluated. May differ from execution_timestamp if the rule evaluates historical or point-in-time data.

attributes.name: data_trust_score
attributes.description: Calculated trust score for the target data product based on this rule execution result, ranging from 0.00 (no trust) to 100.00 (full trust). Aggregated across multiple rules to produce product-level trust metrics.

attributes.name: execution_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Time taken to execute the data quality rule against the target data product, measured in seconds. Used for performance monitoring and optimization.

attributes.name: execution_error_message
attributes.description: Technical error message if the rule execution failed or encountered issues. Null if execution completed successfully.

attributes.name: execution_status
attributes.description: Technical execution status of the rule run: completed (rule executed successfully), failed (execution error), timeout (exceeded time limit), cancelled (manually stopped).

attributes.name: execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the data quality rule was executed against the target data product. Represents the business event time of the quality check.

attributes.name: failure_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of records that failed the quality check, calculated as (records_failed_count / records_evaluated_count) * 100. Used for trend analysis and SLA monitoring.

attributes.name: failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why records failed the quality check (e.g., 'Email format invalid', 'Value exceeds maximum threshold', 'Required field is null').

attributes.name: notification_sent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an alert notification was sent to data stewards or stakeholders for this quality check result. True if notification sent, False otherwise.

attributes.name: pass_fail_status
attributes.description: Overall outcome of the rule execution: pass (within acceptable threshold), fail (exceeds threshold), warning (approaching threshold), error (execution failure).

attributes.name: previous_failure_rate_percent
attributes.description: Failure rate from the previous execution of this rule against the same target product. Used for trend analysis and detecting quality degradation.

attributes.name: records_evaluated_count
attributes.description: Total number of records in the target data product that were evaluated by this rule execution.

attributes.name: records_failed_count
attributes.description: Number of records that failed the data quality rule criteria and did not meet the expected quality threshold.

attributes.name: records_passed_count
attributes.description: Number of records that passed the data quality rule criteria.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Action taken in response to the quality check result: none (no action required), alert_sent (notification to data steward), ticket_created (incident logged), auto_corrected (automated fix applied), quarantined (records isolated), rejected (records blocked from downstream).

attributes.name: remediation_owner

attributes.name: sample_failed_keys

attributes.name: schedule_type

attributes.name: severity_level

attributes.name: sla_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the data quality result meets the defined SLA threshold for this rule and target product. True if within SLA, False if SLA violated.

attributes.name: trend_direction

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

products.name: kpi_dimensionality
products.description: This association product represents the configuration relationship between KPI definitions and the metric dimensions by which they can be sliced and analyzed. It captures the explicit business rules governing which dimensions are available for each KPI, how they aggregate, and their display behavior in BI tools. Each record links one KPI definition to one metric dimension with configuration attributes that exist only in the context of this specific KPI-dimension pairing.. Existence Justification: In retail analytics operations, BI teams actively configure which dimensions are available for each KPI, how they aggregate, their display order, and drill-down behavior. This is not a derived analytical correlation but an explicit configuration that semantic layer architects manage as part of OLAP cube design and BI tool setup. The business recognizes this as 'KPI dimensionality configuration' - a managed artifact that determines how business users can slice and filter metrics.

products.name: report_composition
products.description: This association product represents the configuration relationship between KPI definitions and report definitions in the retail analytics catalog. It captures how KPIs are composed into reports with report-specific presentation rules, display ordering, visualization preferences, and threshold overrides. Each record links one KPI definition to one report definition with attributes that control how that specific KPI appears and behaves within that specific report context.. Existence Justification: In retail analytics operations, BI teams actively manage the composition of reports by selecting which KPIs to include, configuring how each KPI is visualized, setting display order, and defining report-specific presentation rules. A single KPI (e.g., Comparable Store Sales) appears in multiple reports (Executive Dashboard, Store Operations Report, Regional Performance Report) with different visualizations, thresholds, and filters. Conversely, each report contains multiple KPIs arranged in a specific sequence with report-specific configuration. This is an operational configuration activity managed through BI catalog tools, not an analytical correlation.

products.name: metric_entity_dependency
products.description: This association product represents the metadata lineage relationship between semantic metrics and the semantic layer entities they depend on for calculation. It captures the technical join configuration, filter logic, and aggregation behavior required to compute each metric from its constituent entities. Each record links one semantic metric to one semantic layer entity with attributes that define how the entity participates in the metric calculation within the BI semantic layer platform.. Existence Justification: In retail semantic layer platforms (Looker, dbt Semantic Layer, Databricks Unity Catalog), metrics explicitly depend on multiple entities for calculation (e.g., a Gross Margin % metric requires sales_fact, product_dim, and cost_dim entities), and entities are reused across many metrics. The business actively manages these dependencies as metadata configurations that drive BI query generation, defining join paths, filter logic, and aggregation roles for each metric-entity pair.

products.name: sla_kpi_measurement
products.description: This association product represents the measurement contract between supply chain SLA definitions and enterprise KPI definitions. It captures the specific measurement parameters, thresholds, and penalty structures that apply when a particular KPI is used to evaluate a particular SLA. Each record links one SLA definition to one KPI definition with measurement-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this monitoring relationship.. Existence Justification: In retail supply chain operations, a single SLA (e.g., Supplier Fill Rate SLA) is measured by multiple KPIs (fill rate percentage, order completeness count, line item accuracy), and each enterprise KPI (e.g., On-Time Delivery %) is used to measure multiple SLAs across different suppliers, product categories, and distribution centers. The business actively manages SLA performance scorecards where each KPI-SLA pairing has its own measurement frequency, threshold, penalty rate, and effective dates.

attributes.name: record_retention_years

attributes.name: regulatory_authority

attributes.name: supply_chain_program_included

attributes.name: verification_activities_summary

products.description: Individual Critical Control Point (CCP) or Preventive Control defined within a food safety plan. Each food safety plan contains multiple control points that must be monitored and documented during food handling operations.

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.name: approved_by_pcqi

attributes.name: control_point_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code for the control point used in operational documentation and audit trails (e.g., CCP-001, PC-ALLER-05).

attributes.name: control_point_name
attributes.description: Business name of the critical control point or preventive control (e.g., Cooking Temperature Control, Metal Detection, Allergen Cleaning Verification).

attributes.name: control_point_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the control point within the food safety plan. Active control points are currently enforced. Inactive or archived control points are no longer in use but retained for historical compliance records.

attributes.name: control_point_type
attributes.description: Classification of the control point within the food safety management system. Critical Control Points (CCPs) are points where control is essential to prevent or eliminate a food safety hazard. Preventive controls are broader risk-based measures.

attributes.name: corrective_action_procedure
attributes.description: Documented procedure to be followed when monitoring indicates a deviation from the critical limit. Includes steps to identify cause, correct the deviation, prevent recurrence, and handle affected product.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this control point record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for regulatory compliance and change management.

attributes.name: critical_limit_parameter
attributes.description: The measurable parameter that defines the boundary of safety for this control point (e.g., Temperature, Time, pH, Water Activity, Metal Detection Sensitivity, Chlorine Concentration).

attributes.name: critical_limit_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the critical limit value (e.g., degrees Fahrenheit, degrees Celsius, minutes, hours, pH units, ppm, mm).

attributes.name: critical_limit_value
attributes.description: The specific threshold value that must be met or maintained to ensure food safety (e.g., 165°F minimum, pH below 4.6, 2 hours maximum, 1.5mm ferrous detection). May include ranges or multiple conditions.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this control point became or will become operational and enforceable within the food safety plan.

attributes.name: environmental_monitoring_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control point includes environmental monitoring for pathogens (e.g., Listeria in ready-to-eat food production environments). Required for certain high-risk food categories.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this control point is scheduled to be reviewed, updated, or retired. Null if the control point has no planned end date. Supports periodic revalidation requirements.

attributes.name: gfsi_scheme_alignment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) Scheme Alignment
attributes.description: Identifies which GFSI-benchmarked certification scheme this control point supports (e.g., SQF, BRC, FSSC 22000, IFS). Used when facility maintains third-party food safety certifications.

tag_set.value: Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) Scheme Alignment

attributes.name: hazard_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific food safety hazard being controlled at this point (e.g., Survival of Salmonella in raw poultry, Cross-contamination of allergens during packaging, Metal fragments from equipment wear).

attributes.name: hazard_type
attributes.description: Category of food safety hazard addressed by this control point. Biological hazards include pathogens (Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli). Chemical hazards include pesticides, cleaning agents, toxins. Physical hazards include metal, glass, plastic. Allergens are a special category of chemical hazards.

attributes.name: last_validation_date
attributes.description: Date when the control point was last validated to ensure it effectively controls the identified hazard. FDA FSMA requires revalidation at least every 3 years or when significant changes occur.

attributes.name: likelihood_level
attributes.description: Probability that the hazard will occur if the control point is not properly managed. Combined with severity to determine overall risk level.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who last modified this control point record. Supports accountability and change management for food safety plan modifications.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this control point record was last modified. Any change to critical limits, monitoring procedures, or corrective actions must be documented with timestamp for audit trail.

attributes.name: monitoring_equipment
attributes.description: Specific equipment or instruments used to perform monitoring (e.g., Digital probe thermometer Model XYZ, Metal detector Unit 5, pH meter, ATP luminometer). Supports calibration and maintenance tracking.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: How often the control point must be monitored and measured (e.g., Continuous, Every batch, Every 2 hours, Daily, Per shift, Each production run).

attributes.name: monitoring_method
attributes.description: The procedure or technique used to measure and verify the critical limit (e.g., Calibrated thermometer reading, Metal detector scan, Visual inspection, ATP swab test, pH meter measurement, Time-temperature recording).

attributes.name: next_validation_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required validation of this control point. Used for compliance tracking and audit preparation.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional operational notes, special instructions, or contextual information about the control point. May include seasonal variations, equipment-specific considerations, or historical context.

attributes.name: prerequisite_program_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control point is part of a prerequisite program (basic conditions and activities necessary to maintain a hygienic environment) rather than a process-specific preventive control.

attributes.name: process_step
attributes.description: The specific step in the food production or handling process where this control point is applied (e.g., Receiving, Cooking, Cooling, Packaging, Storage, Distribution).

attributes.name: record_keeping_requirement
attributes.description: Documentation requirements for this control point including what records must be maintained, format, retention period, and storage location. Supports regulatory compliance and audit trails.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Specific regulatory citation or standard that mandates or guides this control point (e.g., FDA 21 CFR 117.135, USDA 9 CFR 417, Codex CAC/RCP 1-1969, GFSI requirement).

attributes.name: responsible_role
attributes.description: Job role or position responsible for monitoring this control point (e.g., Line Supervisor, Quality Technician, Receiving Manager, Sanitation Lead). Used for training and accountability.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Risk severity classification of the hazard controlled by this point. Critical severity indicates potential for serious adverse health consequences or death. Used for risk prioritization and resource allocation.

attributes.name: supplier_control_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control point is part of the supply chain preventive controls program, addressing hazards in incoming raw materials and ingredients through supplier verification.

attributes.name: validation_method
attributes.description: Scientific or technical approach used to validate that the control point effectively controls the hazard (e.g., Challenge study, Inoculation study, Literature review, Historical data analysis, Predictive modeling).

attributes.name: verification_frequency
attributes.description: How often verification activities must be performed (e.g., Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Before each production run).

attributes.name: verification_procedure
attributes.description: Methods used to verify that the control point is working as intended. May include calibration checks, record review, testing, audits, and validation studies.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional notes, observations, or context related to the monitoring activity, deviation, or corrective action. Provides supplementary information for audit and investigation purposes.

attributes.name: control_point_type
attributes.description: Classification of the control point monitored: CCP (Critical Control Point per HACCP), CP (Control Point), or PRP (Prerequisite Program). Determines the level of regulatory scrutiny and corrective action requirements.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a corrective action was required due to critical limit deviation or other food safety concern.

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Detailed description of the corrective action taken in response to a critical limit deviation or food safety concern. Required for regulatory compliance and audit documentation.

attributes.name: corrective_action_timestamp

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: critical_limit_upper

attributes.name: deviation_severity

attributes.name: equipment_code

attributes.name: instrument_code

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: limit_status

attributes.name: measured_value

attributes.name: monitoring_employee_name

attributes.name: monitoring_method
attributes.description: Method used to perform the monitoring activity: manual measurement, automated sensor, calibrated instrument, or visual inspection. Impacts data reliability and audit requirements.

attributes.name: monitoring_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the food safety monitoring activity was performed. Critical for establishing compliance timeline and traceability.

attributes.name: product_affected

attributes.name: product_disposition

attributes.name: record_status

attributes.name: unit_of_measure

attributes.name: verification_signature
attributes.description: Electronic or digitized signature of the supervisor verifying the monitoring record. Required for regulatory compliance and audit trail integrity.

attributes.name: verification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the supervisor verification was completed. Establishes timeline for management oversight and compliance review.
